theoretical_positioning.note: Text-embedding literature, text-based rather than network-based (T1). 'Goes beyond prior studies by adding geographic and temporal resolution' is the extension half of T3; agreement with the earlier right-leaning finding not stated. No T0.
Groups use different lexicons, so topic-conditioning makes dissimilarity a proxy (p.4): I7 placed here, as the earlier judge did with a like entry.

The C-index as the measure of inter-party separation in embedding space: method (E2), not a framework. 'Tradition of clustering-based indices' is loose but the paper calls it 'a robust clustering measure'; not flagged.
Complement to lexicon strategies, alternative to network approaches given data restrictions.
